title: Cross-slice relay strategy verification and user-facing documentation
observed_behavior_before: Relay strategy implementation evidence existed in per-slice PSTF directories, but no epic-level artifact mapped the acceptance focus across bahia-8epx.1 through bahia-8epx.10.

User-facing and protocol docs covered most relay taxonomy decisions, but some rollout/setup docs still referred to legacy discovery kind 31974 as current bootstrap evidence and some docs had thin NIP-11/NIP-66/10050 follow-up wording.
Optional NIP-11, NIP-66, and DM relay-list work was plan-scoped but not bounded by dedicated follow-up Beads.

The follow-up Beads bahia-8epx.11.5 and bahia-8epx.11.6 were open planning tasks: resolver NIP-11 metadata was log-only, browser NIP-11 health lacked explicit malformed/limiting cases, and NIP-66 monitor events were not ingested behind configured monitor trust.
The follow-up Bead bahia-8epx.11.7 was open: NIP-51 kind 10050 DM relay-list behavior was reserved for DM-enabled features but not implemented or tested.
intended_behavior: Cross-slice PSTF artifacts map relay strategy acceptance criteria to deterministic tests and documentation evidence for distinct browser, ContextVM, service, repository, operator, AUTH, NIP-65, NIP-86, and SoulFactory/ngit relay behavior.

User-facing and protocol docs describe ContextVM discovery 11316-11320 plus NIP-51 30002 as canonical bootstrap, NIP-65 10002 as advisory, NIP-34 repository relay hints as repository-specific preference, and NIP-86 as opt-in relay-owner HTTP administration only.
Optional NIP-11/NIP-66 metadata and NIP-51 10050 DM relay-list behavior remains advisory, disabled by default, and tracked in Beads rather than prose-only follow-up.
No implementation epic from bahia-8epx.1 through bahia-8epx.10 is reopened unless a blocking verification gap is found.

The bahia-8epx.11.5 and bahia-8epx.11.6 slices implement advisory-only NIP-11 health metadata and configured-trust NIP-66 monitor ingestion without changing Bahia service pubkey trust, configured relay policy, or DM relay-list scope.

The bahia-8epx.11.7 slice implements explicit notification DM service-identity kind 10050 relay-list publication with no default publication and no inference from browser, ContextVM, or service relay sets.

included: PSTF cross-slice acceptance and test matrix artifacts
Verification report naming commands, dates, results, plan items, and covered Beads
User-facing/protocol documentation updates for relay strategy behavior and optional follow-up boundaries
Creation of bounded follow-up Beads for advisory NIP-11, configured-trust NIP-66, and DM relay-list slices
Implementation and deterministic tests for advisory NIP-11 metadata and configured-trust NIP-66 10166/30166 monitor ingestion
Implementation and deterministic tests for explicit notification DM service-identity NIP-51 10050 relay-list publication
excluded: Production implementation changes for completed epics bahia-8epx.1 through bahia-8epx.10
Automatic relay administration reconciliation or UI/CLI workflows
Default trust in NIP-66 monitors or default DM relay-list publication
DM relay-list support for non-notification features or identities other than the Bahia service identity
